datasets.name: Landslide dataset of Iburi district, Japan
datasets.verbatim: The landslide dataset was generated from visual interpretation based on the 3 m resolution Planet images... Finally, 9295 landslides have been visually interpreted based on ArcMap10.6, with a total area of 30.96 km2 [58]

datasets.name: Planet images (3 m resolution)
datasets.verbatim: The landslide dataset was generated from visual interpretation based on the 3 m resolution Planet images... We are grateful to Planet Company for providing us with the images.

datasets.name: Landslide drone images
datasets.verbatim: To avoid misidentification of landslides, we referred to landslide drone images released by the Geospatial Information Agency of Japan regarding this earthquake.

datasets.name: ResNet50 pre-trained weights
datasets.verbatim: In addition, the robust pre−trained weights of ResNet50 on ImageNet were introduced to accelerate convergence and avert dying ReLu [64].

datasets.name: Training samples (partial)
datasets.verbatim: The complete structure of ResNet50 and part of training samples are available. This data can be found here: [https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1x7umIkEnKqZlXS7KSmzDqQRPUWsfQPqB?usp=sharing] (accessed on 12 March 2022).

methods.name: U-Net++ with ResNet50 backbone
methods.summary: A U-Net++ semantic segmentation network using ResNet50 as the feature extraction backbone, trained with transfer learning from ImageNet weights, and implemented using the PyTorch framework.
methods.verbatim: The implement of U−Net++ structure construction referred to the source codes compiled in Pytorch On open source project in GitHub [71]... [71] Yakubovskiy, P.; Segmentation Models Pytorch. GitHub Repository. 2020. Available online: https://github.com/qubvel/segmentation_models.pytorch (accessed on 11 March 2022).

reproducibility_assessment: The landslide inventory is partially  provided, and other input datasets are either commercial or lack clear access paths. The custom code is available via a referenced GitHub repository.
